verdict_note: From reading only (no cargo, build or test). Action::Read is wired correctly: the three exhaustive matches (Action::as_str and both From impls in wire.rs) are updated, no other match on the session Action exists in the workspace, a read job never gets write access (web.synchronize derives its action from the same checked plan the work runs, and web.site_report writes nothing but the site lock), and admission passes the action through unchanged. Change link and library-item update are planned, parsed and graph-checked before the first write, restore from in-memory originals on a write failure, and check cancel only before writing, so a cancel never leaves a half-rewritten site. Every new site-wide command is admitted after checks that need no file, before the lock, on the lexically derived site SDOC id (lead Q1), and settles. Two high findings block. F1: web.synchronize keys files by exact spelling, so a file spelled Index.html on one side and index.html on the other is put (or got) with no time comparison and overwrites the newer copy on a case-folding file system, stamped with the older time. F2: web.template_update (and web.instance_param after a template change) silently drops the authored content of an editable region, repeat or parameter that the template renamed or removed, reported only as outcome updated. Five medium: F3 the STU-WEB-094 cut leaves instance locked regions writable, including through this lane's own web.snippet_insert and web.library_item_insert, while a one-line guard in WebHost::edit would close it; F4 the snippet library lives in a per-document sidecar, not the document-independent site resource STU-WEB-099 names; F5 nested optional regions recurse without bound; F6 the V4-06 class (exact spelling) missed three of the lane's own marker-path sites; F7 percent-encoded spellings the engine denies (%2E) are left pointing at `from` with complete=true, and the red tests that proved it were rewritten to pass. Seven low findings: paperwork, reversibility claims, sync gaps and test coverage.

findings.certainty: READ (comparison keys and write path); the rename replacing a case-variant entry follows from NTFS, default APFS and SMB case folding, UNVERIFIED by a run
findings.severity: high (synchronisation overwrites the newer copy of a file; silent, receipt says transferred)
findings.where: crates/hsk-studio-harness-core/src/web_site.rs:3532-3534 (both walks keep exact-case ids), :3543 (the compared set is the union of exact ids), :3570-3571 (each side's stat is looked up by the exact id), :3443-3460 (one side absent gives put or get with no time or size comparison), :3607-3616 (write_replacing, then write_atomic's rename onto the case-variant path), :3620 (the source's older time is set on the copy); Files.folded (:320-321) exists and is not used here
findings.what: Rows are keyed by exact spelling while NTFS, APFS (default) and SMB shares fold case. A file spelled Index.html on one side and index.html on the other becomes two rows, each with one side absent, so each is a put or a get and the newer-than test of STU-WEB-119 never runs. The atomic writer's rename onto the case-variant name replaces the other side's file whatever its time, and set_modified stamps the copy with the source's older time, so the next review reads both as same and the loss stays invisible. In direction both, both rows run and the side that sorts first wins. The same exact-case lookup applies to the files parameter.
findings.scenario: site/Index.html is three days old; remote/index.html was edited on the server an hour ago. web.synchronize {direction: put, apply: true}: row Index.html (local present, remote absent by exact id) is put; row index.html is none. The put replaces remote/index.html with the three-day-old bytes and stamps them three days old; the receipt says transferred, complete=true, and the next review says same. With direction get the mirror image overwrites newer local edits.
findings.fix: Key rows by the ASCII-folded id on both sides (Files.folded). When the two sides spell one file differently, compare them as one file and list the row as sync_case_mismatch (shown for review, never applied), or adopt the destination's spelling and then apply the normal time and size rule. Before any rename, check the destination folder's entries case-folded and never write through a case variant of an existing entry. Fold the files parameter the same way.
findings.test: Red: local Index.html old, remote index.html newer; put with apply leaves the remote bytes and time unchanged and reports the row as sync_case_mismatch (or remote_newer); the mirror for get; the same outcome on a case-sensitive file system (STU-WEB-131 determinism).

findings.severity: high (silent loss of authored instance content across every instance; not an undo step)
findings.where: crates/hsk-studio-harness-core/src/web_site.rs:2343-2350 (Gen::emit writes an editable's content only for a name the template still has), :2356-2366 (repeat entries looked up by the template's repeat names), :2385 (only the template's parameters are carried), :2413-2421 (standing: an instance whose locked text equals its baseline is TemplateChanged whatever changed), :2766 (TemplateChanged gives outcome updated and is written), :2786 (the receipt row carries byte ranges only); :2688-2697 (instance_edit allows TemplateChanged and regenerates from the template on disk)
findings.what: STU-WEB-093 propagates template changes, but the content an operator wrote in an instance's editable region belongs to the instance. When the template renames or removes an editable region (or a repeat, or a parameter), the regenerated instance has no slot for the old content and it is dropped. The receipt reports outcome updated with byte ranges; nothing names the lost region, and web.template_update is not a web.undo step, so the text is gone from every instance at once. web.instance_param or web.instance_repeat on an instance whose template changed does the same inside a step labelled Set Instance Parameter or Edit Repeating Region (undoable, but it silently applies the pending template change too).
findings.scenario: Templates/main.dwt has the editable region main; a.html and b.html hold authored text in main. The template is edited to <!-- TemplateBeginEditable name='content' --> in its place. web.template_update {template: Templates/main.dwt}: both instances are TemplateChanged, outcome updated; their main text is replaced by the template's default content; receipt complete=true.
findings.fix: Before writing, compare the instance's editable names (top level and per repeat entry), repeat names and parameter names with the template's. Any instance content with no slot makes the outcome regions_orphaned (code template_region_orphaned, severity warning, naming the document and the regions), reported and not written, as drift is, with a resolve option (for example discard, or a map from old to new name). instance_edit refuses the same code before regenerating. Dreamweaver's own behaviour here is UNVERIFIED (D5).
findings.test: Red: two instances carry authored text in main; the template renames main to content; web.template_update leaves both files byte for byte and reports regions_orphaned naming main; with the chosen resolve the text lands in content; web.instance_param on such an instance refuses the same code.

findings.severity: medium (spec MUST [STU-WEB-094]/[STU-WEB-159] cut while its fix is one line at the shared choke point; this lane's own insert paths write locked text)
findings.where: crates/hsk-studio-harness-core/src/web_commands.rs:479-489 (WebHost::edit: every source edit goes through it: the six mutating rows at :303-339, and this lane's web.library_item_insert at web_site.rs:2831, web.snippet_insert at :3410 and instance_edit at :2697); web_site.rs:2261-2286 (instance_of already computes each editable content range); :2690-2692 and :2768-2772 (what drift causes afterwards)
findings.what: STU-WEB-094 and STU-WEB-159: a text edit inside a locked region of an instance MUST be refused with a typed error naming the region and the owning template, offering detach. With the cut, web.set_text, web.set_attribute, web.remove_attribute, web.insert_element, web.insert_fragment, web.remove_node, and this lane's own web.snippet_insert and web.library_item_insert, write an instance's locked text without a word. The instance then reads drifted (locked_changed): web.instance_param and web.instance_repeat refuse template_instance_drift, web.template_update skips it, and the only remedies are reapply, which discards the edit, or detach. The cut note says the refusal needs the web.set_text and insert paths in web_commands.rs; the two lane-owned insert paths are in web_site.rs, and all paths meet in WebHost::edit.
findings.scenario: A model opens a.html (an instance) and runs web.set_attribute on the h1, which is locked: accepted and saved. The next web.instance_param refuses template_instance_drift; web.template_update reports a.html drifted; reapply loses the attribute. web.snippet_insert at an offset inside the locked head behaves the same.
findings.fix: web_site.rs: pub(super) fn locked_refusal(doc, edits, label) -> R<()>: when instance_of(doc) is Some, every edit span must lie inside one editable content range (ends inclusive), else refuse template_edit_in_locked_region (severity error; detail {region, template, remedy: [detach]}); exempt the two instance_edit labels, which regenerate locked text by design. web_commands.rs: one call line at the top of WebHost::edit (a fourth hunk; lead approval). Undo and redo go through step_back, not edit, so recorded steps still replay.
findings.test: Red: on an instance, web.set_attribute on the h1, web.snippet_insert inside head and web.library_item_insert under body outside an editable region each refuse template_edit_in_locked_region naming the template; web.set_text on #lead (editable) is accepted; web.instance_param still works.

findings.severity: medium (STU-WEB-099: the trigger map is not a document-independent site resource; triggers are unique per record, not per site; library changes are lost on open)
findings.where: crates/hsk-studio-harness-core/src/web_commands.rs:1086-1089 (sidecar: <page>.studio-site.json beside one document), :432-440 (web.open replaces self.site with that document's record, none if absent, with no unsaved check), :578-582 (web.save writes the record beside the saved document only), :269 (dirty compares the document bytes only), :273 (state_json carries site_json); crates/hsk-studio-harness-core/src/web_site.rs:3319-3347 (web.snippet edits self.site), :3289-3299 (uniqueness within that one record), :3219 (with_depth puts every snippet with both insert texts into site_json)
findings.what: STU-WEB-099 makes the trigger map a document-independent site resource with triggers unique within a site. Here the library lives in the site record saved beside whichever page was open. A second page of the same site opens with no record (web.snippets and web.snippet_insert refuse no_site) or with its own copy, so two copies can claim one trigger for different snippets and each passes unique_triggers. A web.snippet change leaves dirty false, so a model that checks dirty and then opens another page loses it without warning. Also, every web command result and op record carries the whole library with its insert texts through state_json (up to the 1 MiB record), while web.snippets deliberately omits them.
findings.scenario: Open index.html, web.site, web.snippet {folder_path: Markup, snippet_name: Bullets, trigger: ul}, web.save. Open about.html (no record): web.snippets refuses no_site. web.site again, web.snippet {folder_path: Markup, snippet_name: Underline, trigger: ul}, web.save: accepted. The site now holds two libraries with one trigger for two snippets; neither refuses snippet_trigger_duplicate.
findings.fix: Keep the site record (with snippets and the STU-WEB-113 fields) once per site, for example a reserved record at local_root that every web.open inside local_root reads, and refuse or reconcile a per-document record that disagrees. Count a site-record change in dirty, or write it at the step. Return the library in state_json without insert texts (as web.snippets does). If the per-document record stays in this lane, declare it in the manual and the lane notes as a gap against STU-WEB-099 and STU-WEB-113.
findings.test: Red: two pages of one site; a snippet defined while editing one is listed while editing the other; a duplicate trigger defined from the second page refuses snippet_trigger_duplicate naming both; a web.snippet step sets dirty; a web.read result carries no insert text.

findings.certainty: READ (the missing depth bound); whether 2047 frames overflow depends on build profile and thread stack, UNVERIFIED, not run
findings.severity: medium (V4-01/02: hostile template can abort the process instead of a typed refusal)
findings.where: crates/hsk-studio-harness-core/src/web_site.rs:2097-2109 (TemplateBeginIf may nest without limit; only editable-in-editable and repeat-in-repeat are refused), :1894 (MAX_MARKERS = 4096 is the only bound), recursion in checked_parts :2174-2197, Template::repeat :2021-2027 and Gen::emit :2328-2373
findings.what: template_of reads markers with an explicit stack, but the Part tree it builds is then walked recursively. A .dwt with one boolean parameter and 2047 nested optional regions stays under the 4096-marker cap (about 120 KB) and drives checked_parts and Gen::emit 2047 frames deep. web.template_regions, web.template_instance, web.instance_param, web.instance_repeat and web.template_update all reach these walks. A stack overflow aborts the process: no panic, no typed refusal, no terminal frame. Windows main threads have 1 MiB of stack and test threads 2 MiB, and debug frames of emit carry format! temporaries.
findings.scenario: site/Templates/deep.dwt: <!-- TemplateParam name='b' type='boolean' value='true' -->, then 2047 times <!-- TemplateBeginIf cond='b' -->, then x, then 2047 times <!-- TemplateEndIf -->. web.template_regions {path: Templates/deep.dwt}.
findings.fix: Bound region depth while reading: when the stack grows past a small limit (32, as MAX_SEGMENTS), refuse template_nesting_too_deep naming document:line, so every recursive walk is bounded by construction (or make the walks iterative). Declare the bound in the manual.
findings.test: Hostile test with 2047 nested optional regions: typed refusal, no abort; a template at the bound still reads.

findings.severity: medium (V4-06 count mismatch; silent partial propagation of a template or library item)
findings.where: crates/hsk-studio-harness-core/src/web_site.rs:2735 (template_update includes an instance only when i.template == template, exact), :2258 (instance_of: a template path that is not a portable root path, e.g. percent-encoded, refuses template_markup_invalid; template_update calls it with ? on every page at :2734-2738, so one such page aborts every template update of the site), :2579 (marker_targets: the report's referenced set uses the marker text as spelled), :2859 (library_item_update compares library_target(..) with the item exactly), :2587-2589 (library_target does not percent-decode); S/builders/lanes/hsk-studio-web-site-2.json:144-172 (v4_06 lists six sites, none of these)
findings.what: The lane named the class 'a reference compared by exact spelling where any spelling of the same file must match' and fixed it for engine references, but its own marker references (InstanceBegin template, #BeginLibraryItem) still compare exactly. An instance naming its template in another letter case is skipped by web.template_update (not updated, not reported as drifted, absent from the receipt), and its template is listed file_orphaned by web.site_report. A document holding a library item spelled in another case is skipped by web.library_item_update, which reports complete=true. STU-WEB-093 and STU-WEB-096 ('updates every instance', 'updates every reference') silently do not.
findings.scenario: Templates/main.dwt exists; old.html holds <!-- InstanceBegin template='/templates/Main.dwt' -->. web.template_update {template: Templates/main.dwt}: old.html is not in the receipt. If it is the template's only instance, web.site_report lists Templates/main.dwt as file_orphaned. A page with <!-- #BeginLibraryItem '/library/Nav.lbi' --> is not updated by web.library_item_update {item: Library/nav.lbi}.
findings.fix: Resolve marker paths through the same lookup as engine references: decoded_path, then Files.folded. An exact match is the item; a folded match is the item plus a case_mismatch row in the receipt (or a typed refusal naming document:line); a marker path that cannot be resolved is a receipt row naming document:line, not an abort of the whole site. Add the three sites to the lane's V4-06 list.
findings.test: Red: one instance spelled /templates/Main.dwt and one document holding /library/Nav.lbi; web.template_update and web.library_item_update update them with a case_mismatch row, or refuse naming them, and never omit them; web.site_report does not list the template as orphaned.

findings.certainty: READ, and RUN by the lane: focused-smb-web-site-2-70f64b55.log shows old%2Ehtml?q=1 denied as ambiguous_path
findings.severity: medium (silent link breakage with complete=true; residual of review e3fc0e89 F2; the red tests that proved it were rewritten to pass)
findings.where: crates/hsk-studio-harness-core/src/web_site.rs:1510-1516 (plan: in a document that does not move, a Denied reach falls to continue), :527-534 (reaches matches only File, Case and Missing), :112-114 (manual: the engine denies %2E, %2F and %5C as ambiguous_path); commit dccc57b2: crates/hsk-studio-harness/tests/web_site_depth.rs:140 and :176 (old%2Ehtml and thanks%2Ehtml replaced by ol%64.html and th%61nks.html)
findings.what: old%2Ehtml names old.html on common servers (the server decodes %2E), and a reference through a non-portable folder (My Folder/../old.html) reaches it in a browser too. Both are Denied in the site graph, so web.change_link and web.move_file leave them naming the old path and report complete=true. Review e3fc0e89 F2 named this residual for documents that do not move ('a denied spelling of from, such as thanks%2Ehtml, is never rewritten'); the F2 ruling covered only the moved document. The lane's red tests asserted these spellings are rewritten; when they failed at 70f64b55, dccc57b2 changed the inputs to spellings the engine passes. The 'every spelling' claim is now proven only for the spellings the implementation already handles.
findings.scenario: index.html holds <a href='old%2Ehtml'>. web.change_link {from: old.html, to: news.html}: receipt complete=true; the link still names old.html. The same holds for web.move_file of thanks.html with thanks%2Ehtml elsewhere in the site.
findings.fix: In plan, for a Denied reference in any document, decode its path leniently (percent_decoded) and resolve it lexically (lexical or denied_place); if it names `from` (folded), rewrite it as a reached reference, or refuse reference_not_rewritable naming document:line. At minimum, list such references in the receipt as left_denied with complete=false. Restore the original red inputs.
findings.test: Restore old%2Ehtml and thanks%2Ehtml in change_link_rewrites_every_spelling_site_wide and a_move_rewrites_case_mismatched_and_percent_encoded_spellings: each is rewritten or refused typed, never complete=true with the reference unchanged.

findings.severity: low (V4-07: reversibility claims that no longer hold; no undo for site-wide rewrites)
findings.where: crates/hsk-studio-harness-core/src/web_site.rs:66-67 ('a reverse move restores the bytes'), :122-123 ('the reverse change restores the bytes'), :1511 (every spelling of `from` rewritten to the one canonical spelling), :1764-1766 (link_target_missing when the reverse change's target is a missing page)
findings.what: A move now rewrites case-mismatched and percent-encoded spellings to one canonical spelling, so a reverse move writes the canonical spelling, not the bytes it replaced. web.change_link merges the references to `from` with those that already name `to`; its reverse also rewrites links that named `to` before, and when `from` was a missing page the reverse is refused link_target_missing. Neither command is a web.undo step, so the receipt is the only way back, and nothing applies it.
findings.scenario: index.html links Old.html (old.html missing) and news.html. web.change_link {from: old.html, to: news.html} rewrites one link. The reverse {from: news.html, to: old.html} refuses link_target_missing. With old.html present, the reverse rewrites both links, including the one that named news.html before.
findings.fix: Weaken both claims to what holds ('the receipt names every changed range and its original reference'), or add a revert from a receipt that applies the ranges in reverse when each file still holds the receipt's after bytes, else refuses receipt_stale.
findings.test: If a revert is added: change link, revert from the receipt, files byte-identical; a file changed since refuses receipt_stale.

findings.certainty: READ; (b) depends on the engine's CSS url tokenizing, UNVERIFIED
findings.severity: low (change-link gaps: no repair for case_mismatch rows; raw parentheses in an unquoted CSS url)
findings.where: crates/hsk-studio-harness-core/src/web_site.rs:530 (a Case reach reaches `from` only when its actual file is `from`), :1748 (from == to refused before admission), :1523-1524 (the new path is written raw over the path bytes); crates/hsk-studio-harness-core/src/web_commands.rs:970-979 (portable names may hold ( ) , + @ ~)
findings.what: (a) web.site_report lists case_mismatch rows (About.html when the file is about.html), but no web.change_link repairs them: {from: About.html, to: about.html} finds no reference, because the reach's actual file is about.html, not `from`, and refuses nothing_to_change after admission and the lock; {from: about.html, to: about.html} refuses nothing_to_change before admission. (b) A target name holding ( or ) is written raw into an unquoted CSS url(...). In CSS Syntax a ( inside an unquoted url makes a bad-url token and ) ends it. Verification re-scans the sheet, so a tokenizer that follows CSS Syntax refuses move_rewrite_unverified (the move or change cannot be done at all); a lenient one lets broken CSS be written.
findings.scenario: (a) The report's case_mismatch row index.html -> About.html; the model runs web.change_link {from: About.html, to: about.html} and gets nothing_to_change. (b) styles/site.css holds url(img/bg.png); web.move_file {from: img/bg.png, to: img/bg(1).png}.
findings.fix: (a) When `from` folds to an existing file spelled differently, count references whose requested id equals `from` (Reach::Case { id }) as reaching it, so {from: About.html, to: about.html} normalises the spelling. (b) For an unquoted CSS url whose new path holds a character outside the url-safe set, write url("...") with the path escaped as a CSS string, or refuse reference_not_rewritable.
findings.test: (a) A case_mismatch row repaired by web.change_link, report clean afterwards. (b) A sheet with url(img/bg.png) and a move to img/bg(1).png: the sheet reads url("img/bg(1).png"), or the move refuses typed.

findings.where: crates/hsk-studio-harness-core/src/web_site.rs:3582-3588 (the review result carries no digest of its action list), :3589-3602 (apply recomputes the comparison from scratch), :3589-3597 (only a get onto the open document's unsaved edits refuses), :3443-3478 (no content hash: within 2 s and the same size reads same)
findings.what: STU-WEB-119 presents the action list for review, then applies it. Here apply recomputes, so it acts on the state at apply time, not the list the operator or model reviewed; nothing tells the caller the two differ. A put of the open document with unsaved edits silently sends the bytes on disk. Two copies of one size whose times differ by under 2 s read same even when their bytes differ (no hash), so a quick same-size edit after a sync is never transferred.
findings.scenario: Review (put) lists 3 puts; between review and apply the operator edits other.html locally; apply also puts other.html, which the review listed as remote_newer (left alone), and the result does not say the plan changed. Separately: index.html open with unsaved edits; web.synchronize {direction: put, apply: true} sends the saved bytes, and the receipt says transferred.
findings.fix: Return a plan digest with the review and accept it on apply (refuse sync_plan_changed when the recomputed list differs); refuse document_unsaved for a put of the dirty open document too; when sizes match and times are within the tolerance, compare SHA-256 before calling them same.
findings.test: Apply with a stale plan digest refuses sync_plan_changed; a put of the dirty open document refuses document_unsaved; two same-size copies within 2 s with different bytes are not same.

answers.action_read_wiring: Correct. Exhaustive matches: Action::as_str (ports.rs), From<Action> for ActionWire and From<ActionWire> for Action (wire.rs): all three updated; a workspace grep finds no other match on the session Action (every other hit constructs a value). Downstream crates outside this workspace: NOT_INSPECTED. No write leak: web.site_report and a synchronize review write nothing but the site lock; synchronize derives read, export or edit from the same SyncPlan the work runs (web_site.rs:1729-1737), so a review can never apply. Admission: JobLifecycle, AdmissionJobPort and the viewer's job_binding pass the action through and treat no action specially; a host keyed by exact action needs a read grant (F10).
answers.rewrites: Quoting: a reference whose bytes equal its decoded text gets its path bytes replaced; otherwise the whole attribute value is rewritten through escape_attr and always quoted (review e3fc0e89 F3 fix kept); portable names hold no quote, whitespace or ampersand; unquoted CSS url with ( ) is F9. Traversal: from and to go through site_path (no .., absolute, UNC, backslash, ADS or device names); to must be a walked file and links are never walked files; lone_source and web.template_instance check the resolved path under the resolved root. Case folding: engine references fold (reaches, Files.spelled); marker references do not (F6); synchronisation does not (F1). Partial failure: change link and library-item update write each file atomically, stop at the first failure and restore every written file from the in-memory originals with a receipt; template update is one transaction per instance, as STU-WEB-093 says, and a rerun converges; cancel is checked through planning and before the first write, never between writes, so a cancel leaves no half-rewritten site. A process crash between files leaves a partial rewrite and a stale lock with no journal (the model review e3fc0e89 accepted for moves). Undo: none (F8). JobPort: web.change_link, web.template_update and web.library_item_update are admitted as edit, and web.synchronize by mode, after checks that need no file, before lock and walk, on the lexically derived site SDOC id (lead Q1); each settles completed, canceled or failed with its code, and an accepted result carries job.
answers.synchronize: Never deletes: there is no delete path. Put never overwrites a remote copy newer by more than 2 s, get never a newer local copy, and the same time with another size is conflict and left alone, except for the case-variant path of F1. Two-way is newest-wins with no sync baseline, so a file changed on both sides loses the older side's edit (lead question 4). Timestamps: the source's time is kept on the copy (time_kept false when set_modified fails; the next review then sees the copy newer, which is benign). Cancel: checked before each file; each file is one atomic write; a cancel refuses canceled with the receipt so far; transferred files stay (declared).
answers.snippets: Persistence through the per-document site record (F4). Undo: web.snippet records the whole Site before and after as one Change::Site step, so undo and redo restore the library exactly. Uniqueness is enforced on add and replace and on load; a duplicate in a hand-edited record makes web.open of that page refuse site_record_invalid.
answers.stu_web_094_cut: Yes, a correctness hole (F3): locked regions of instances are writable by every source-editing command, including this lane's web.snippet_insert and web.library_item_insert, and the result is a drifted instance whose only remedies discard the edit or detach. Fix size: about 30 lines in web_site.rs (a guard reusing instance_of's editable ranges) and one call line at the top of WebHost::edit in web_commands.rs, a fourth hunk.
answers.host_integration: Typed refusals throughout the code read (slicing goes through get, the windows(2) indexing cannot panic); the one abort path found is F5. Every new row gets a UiDescriptor id through action::ui_seed (studio.command.web-*), and the drive reaches every row through web_commands::row. History steps carry the caller's CommandContext and use the row display names (Set Instance Parameter, Edit Repeating Region, Insert Library Item, Snippet, Insert Snippet, Site Definition). Site-wide receipts carry no actor, only the job's correlation, as for web.move_file in SMB-WEB-SITE-1. The test helpers assert one terminal frame per command. host_integration.jobs is wrong (F11).
answers.web_commands_hunks: Within the approval: the fallthrough to site_command (web_commands.rs:409), which ends in the typed unknown_command (web_site.rs:1739); one depth field on Site; site_from's default literal (forced by the field) and its depth_into call; site_json wrapped by with_depth. read_sidecar needed no edit, because it calls site_from. The stale docs in web_commands.rs (F11) are outside the hunks.
